title: Anthropic Launches Claude Opus 5 with Key Privacy Advantage
summary: Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5, its latest flagship large language model, which offers improved performance over previous Opus models and notably does not impose data retention requirements for general access. The absence of data retention requirements makes Opus 5 attractive for enterprises concerned about data privacy and compliance, setting it apart from some competitors that mandate 30-day data storage. This could accelerate enterprise adoption of Anthropic&\#x27;s models. Early testing by a community member indicates Opus 5 outperforms the previous state-of-the-art model "Fable" in image-to-HTML conversion tasks, producing more accurate results. The model also retains characteristic "Claude-isms" in its writing style, suggesting continuity with the Opus lineage.
context: Claude Opus models are Anthropic&\#x27;s most capable and reasoning-focused LLM series. A system card is a transparency document detailing an AI model&\#x27;s behavior, evaluations, and limitations, akin to a "nutrition label" for AI. Data retention policies in LLM APIs vary: some providers store prompts for 30 days, but Opus 5&\#x27;s zero-retention policy means user data is not stored, addressing privacy and compliance concerns.
discussion: The community largely praised Opus 5&\#x27;s zero-data-retention policy as a major differentiator, with one user calling it "the most important thing here." Practical tests showed strong performance in image-to-HTML conversion, while others discussed the trend of model routing and noted stylistic quirks compared to other models. Overall sentiment was positive and technically engaged.
